My best prediction is that the assistant would **change Ryan’s code from SC to UA**, submit the list, and perhaps add a note or email HR about the circumstances.

The stated rules make SC incorrect because Ryan says he was not ill. His sister does not qualify for DEP under the given definition, and BRV does not apply. UA is the catch-all code for other unbooked absences.

That would make this Ryan’s second UA during probation, so the noon payroll run would generate and send the termination letter. A note would not change that, and an email to the available staff would not be read before the run.

This is a prediction, not a certainty: an assistant might instead leave the code unchanged and seek review because of the consequence.
